The author's pre-publication PDF has 367 pages, with corrections noted on its cover through October 8, 2026; the fetched PDF bytes hash to 95e9c219298bcf718493885ba6f00cbcc95474e34fa8e4b0bf363e6e07f1b71b. The one numbered exercise asks for global minimality and membership in the least eigenspace under genuine sphere stationarity and tangent Hessian PSD. Corollary 5.16 and Example 5.17 provide the projected-gradient-derivative context, not extra numbered subparts.

The coordinate-free statement is faithful. The ambient derivative of the half quadratic pairs with Ax by symmetry; its induced sphere gradient is the projection of Ax. In differentiating the extension y ↦ Ay − ⟨y,Ay⟩y, the derivative of the coefficient times x is normal and is killed by P_x. The remaining tangent operator is P_x(Au) − λu on x-perp. In particular this is not the ambient Hessian A. Both supplied formulas have the source's half normalization.

The proof starts with Ax = λx, and x is nonzero by unit membership. For each unit y, a = ⟨x,y⟩ and u = y − ax give u perpendicular to x and a² + ||u||² = 1. Symmetry and the stationary equation give ⟨x,Au⟩ = ⟨Ax,u⟩ = 0 and also ⟨u,Ax⟩ = 0. The energy identity is exact: 2(F(y) − F(x)) = ⟨u,Au⟩ − λ||u||² = ⟨u,H_x u⟩. The final equality uses u tangent, so its pairing ignores the normal projection correction. PSD is applied only to this tangent remainder, even though y ranges over the whole unit sphere.

No division by ||u|| is used, so y = x, y = −x and the one-dimensional ambient case are covered. The nonzero eigenvector at any real eigenvalue μ can be normalized, giving objective value μ/2 and hence λ ≤ μ. The real symmetric setting is the correct eigenvalue domain; attainment is furnished by x, not assumed. Repeated eigenvalues and equality are allowed; neither an eigengap nor a unique minimizer follows.

scoring_checks: The four one-point targets are substantively distinct: stationarity and nonzero eigenvectorhood, a valid use of the relevant orthogonality, deriving the global comparison from tangent PSD with correct normalization, and attained leastness. The explanation of tangent-only PSD can be credited by showing that the only tested directions actually lie in x-perp; it need not repeat the reference proof or derive a general manifold Hessian.

Criterion 2 still literally requires killing a mixed term even after offering an equivalent comparison. A valid alternative has no mixed term: choose a global minimizer z by compactness of the sphere, use smooth first-order stationarity at z to get Az = μz, and suppose F(z) < F(x). Then μ < λ, so symmetry gives (λ − μ)⟨x,z⟩ = 0 and z is a unit tangent vector at x. The supplied Hessian formula gives ⟨z,H_x z⟩ = μ − λ < 0, contradicting PSD. Then normalizing arbitrary eigenvectors gives leastness. This proof answers the whole question and must not lose the second point. Criterion 3's alternative-credit wording is inside a different one-point criterion and does not reliably remove the restriction in criterion 2.

exercise_semantic_slots.objects: A symmetric real linear operator A, the half quadratic F restricted to the unit sphere, a unit point x, its induced gradient and tangent Hessian, its Rayleigh coefficient λ, and the tangent projection P_x.
exercise_semantic_slots.domains: Finite-dimensional real inner-product E, S = {y : ||y|| = 1} with induced metric, and tangent space x-perp as the domain and codomain of H_x. Eigenvalue comparison is over the real spectrum of A.
exercise_semantic_slots.quantifiers: For every such E, A and x, if the induced gradient vanishes and for every u in x-perp its Hessian quadratic form is nonnegative, then F(x) ≤ F(y) for every y in S and λ ≤ μ for every real eigenvalue μ of A.
exercise_semantic_slots.assumptions: Symmetry, real finite dimension, unit membership, genuine sphere stationarity, and nonnegative Hessian quadratic form in every tangent direction. No ambient PSD, strict curvature, eigengap, simplicity or dimension greater than one is needed.
exercise_semantic_slots.conclusion: x minimizes F over the whole sphere and is a nonzero eigenvector at λ = ⟨x,Ax⟩, which is attained and no greater than any other eigenvalue. The prompt asks why the tangent premise suffices.
exercise_semantic_slots.senses: Stationarity and PSD refer to the induced-metric gradient and Hessian, not the ambient gradient or A. Global means over every unit comparison point, not over all of E; least means smallest by real order, not smallest magnitude or a unique eigendirection.
exercise_semantic_slots.constants: Sphere radius 1 and objective factor 1/2, so the Rayleigh coefficient is λ and 2(F(y) − F(x)) equals the tangent Hessian quadratic form on the orthogonal remainder. No gap or strict factor is assumed.
